calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 4, 25–29 January 2027. Tuesday 26 January 2027, P3. One 40-minute formative lesson for up to five learners. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February, six weeks; Week 6 assessing. Source Week 5 retains its mixed evidence role. No clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: Exact E19 weekly outcome, F19 focus, G19 lesson outcome and J19 evidence retained. H19 sequence and I19 timing retained. Teacher models requirement matching, then learners use an invented job card and a three-state checklist. Source RAG structure is expressed by marks and words: S Shown here, ? Check, N Next step, without colour-only meaning or deficit labels. A short classroom skill task provides possible current evidence without personal records. Support and one improvement target keep routes open. Review is private; K19 websites become prepared cards. Usual aids, reduced choices and model retained; Aspire optional.

sources.note: Physical row 19 is Spring 1 row 4. E19, F19, G19 and J19 verified exactly. H19 sequence and I19 timing retained. Generic invented cards and labelled checklist states replace websites and colour-only RAG. Raw workbook not distributed.

Accepted BUILD Week 3 supplies clean layout, folder shape and retrieval continuity. This lesson uses row 19 outcomes, sequence and evidence. The generic picture bank is reused from accepted Week 2, separately recorded in ASSET_RECORD.

Tuesday 26 January 2027 P3. Exact outcome. Generic attendance, qualification type/level, skill and attitude requirements against invented job cards. No named employer, provider, exam board, qualification title or place. Next steps, never deficits. Same BUILD rules, up to five learners, 40 minutes. Next Weeks 5–6 one per return; further GROW Careers paused. Pause for Downloaded.

source_end_check: Can the student identify one strength and one development need?
source_evidence: Requirement-match checklist and one improvement target.
source_sequence_verbatim: Arrival/retrieval linked to previous careers learning → I Do: explain/model entry requirements and my gaps with concrete examples → We Do: guided sorting/annotating/scenario discussion → You Do: Teacher models requirement matching; use simple RAG checklist for a selected course/job; identify support rather than closing routes prematurely. → 1:1/whole-class review → exit check and add evidence to Careers Portfolio.
timing: Recall that job cards can ask for different skills; use Week 3 or supply a model.
Pre-teach requirement and strength; model A and the three checklist states.
Match A to its evidence; plan support and check that unknown does not mean unable.
Choose B or C; try its short skill task, match evidence and choose one supported improvement target.
Check one evidenced strength and one next step; retain NS and reply; bank checklist and target.

routes.Supported: Read one requirement at a time. Keep the picture, plan, model and word bank. Offer two labels or two next steps. Point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Usual aids stay available; record supplied answers.
routes.Independent: Choose B or C. Try the short skill task with usual aids, match the four requirements to what is known and identify one shown skill plus a next step. Keep the model and source card.
routes.Aspire: Explain why Check is different from not being able to do something. Make the target clearer by naming help, a time and how to check progress. No extra public speech or writing required.

checklist_states.label: Shown here
checklist_states.meaning: There is a clear clue from this task.

checklist_states.label: Check
checklist_states.meaning: We do not know yet. Ask for help to check.

checklist_states.label: Next step
checklist_states.meaning: Choose a small step to practise or find out.

colour_blind_safe: Three states have marks and words. Pictures and captions carry meaning; no colour-only codes.
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, jobs, requirements and the model person are invented and generic. Pictures are generic symbols, not real people or places. Learner classroom work is actual evidence and must not be invented. No employer, provider, exam board, qualification title, place, product or platform named.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No personal grades, attendance history, family jobs or finances requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Either choice can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank fields. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show an adult privately. Exact scribe records words/selections, reads back and allows correction. Separate usual access from supplied answers.
worked_example_and_fade: A asked for help when a word was unclear. Which requirement has a clue? A ask for help; B qualification. Key A. Point to the record if unsure and model the match. Keep pictures, plan, words and normal aids; fade answer cues only.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: four short fields, clear model and reduced-choice states. Communication and Interaction: one instruction, pre-taught words, processing time, frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm stages, choice, pass, supported pause/return; no cold calling. Sensory and Physical: large clear text/pictures, pointing instead of moving cards, no colour-only codes. EAL: plan in any language; read and explain requirement words.
misconceptions: Unknown does not mean unable. One thing to work on does not close a route. A qualification level on an invented card is not a rule for every job. A completed class task does not prove attendance or a qualification. Shown here records a limited observation; further practice can still be useful.

success: Identify one requirement with a relevant clue that it is met in this classroom task.

Keep missing information distinct from inability and record support accurately.

evidence.description: Requirement-match checklist and one improvement target. Keep actual task response, four states, evidenced strength, next step, target/help/time/check, access, prompts, first response, NS and reply.

assessment: Exact source evidence: Requirement-match checklist and one improvement target. Keep selected card, actual ordered response, all four states, one shown requirement and clue, one thing to work on, target/help/time/check, access, prompts, first response, one NS and reply. Judge evidenced strength and next-step identification separately. Usual aids are allowed by the invented skill requirement. Supplied answers do not prove the skill; keep partial evidence and arrange another supported attempt. This is classroom evidence, not proof of real job eligibility.
where_this_leads: This helps me notice what I can do and ask for help with a next step towards work or training.

Point to HELP or ask for a private talk.
Ask a trusted adult or use the school’s help route.
If one adult is busy, ask another adult.
You may pass, pause and return with help.
You do not need to share private records.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Tuesday 26 January 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · BUILD · up to five learners · Spring 1 Week 4 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term. Week 6 assessing; source Week 5 retains its mixed evidence role.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Students compare their current strengths/qualifications with a realistic course, training or job requirement.
I can identify one requirement I already meet and one thing I may need to work on.
Source: BUILD Careers physical row 19 / Spring 1 row 4. E19 weekly outcome, F19 focus, G19 lesson outcome, H19 sequence, I19 timing and J19 evidence.

A requirement is something a role asks for. Match the exact requirement to evidence, then plan support. In this lesson a gap means something to check or practise, never a judgement of worth or a closed route. All job cards and the model person are invented. Generic qualification levels are practice details, not real recruitment rules.

Identify one requirement with a clear clue that it is met in this task. Identify one thing to check or practise and set a small target with help. Keep Shown here, Check and Next step distinct; do not guess about unknown records.

Books, pens, reusable job cards, Vocabulary Mat and evidence record. No real attendance or qualification records. The learner may point to or order words using usual aids; no objects, tools, food or gardening work. Confirm private help and supported pause/return. No internet, login or phone.
This helps me notice what I can do and ask for help with a next step towards work or training.
Recall that job cards can ask for different skills; use Week 3 or supply a model.
Pre-teach requirement and strength; model A and the three checklist states.
Match A to its evidence; plan support and check that unknown does not mean unable.
Choose B or C; try its short skill task, match evidence and choose one supported improvement target.
Check one evidenced strength and one next step; retain NS and reply; bank checklist and target.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes, following I19. Processing time and brief pauses are included. Slides 7 and 8 share the 23–35-minute task window.

0–5: recall a Week 3 entry skill or supply the idea; requirements can differ. 5–9: read the exact outcome; teach requirement, strength, evidence, check and next step. 9–13: model A. The invented person asked for help, so attitude is Shown here. Skill is Next step: practise the three-step plan. Attendance and qualification are Check because facts are absent.

13–19: match A’s four requirements to its record and explain one clue. Offer two states at a time. Model a target naming the action, trusted adult, next lesson and all-three check. 19–23: private hinge on an unknown qualification. Re-model and use the parallel check if unclear. Never change unknown to unable.

23–35: choose B stockroom or C garden. Try the short word-order task in a book, by pointing, typing or exact scribe. Use the supplied plan and usual aids. A correct order can evidence this classroom skill; record actual help and do not silently supply the answer. Build the four-row checklist. Attendance and qualification remain Check without private records. Mark attitude only if observed. Identify one shown requirement and one thing to check or practise further; choose a target with help, a time and a progress check.

35–38: privately check evidence and target; give one NS and retain the reply. 38–40: show one strength and one supported next step. Bank the actual checklist and improvement target in Careers Portfolio. A model-only or unobserved response is partial evidence; allow another supported check later.

Read one requirement at a time. Keep the picture, plan, model and word bank. Offer two labels or two next steps. Point, sign, type or use an exact scribe. Usual aids stay available; record supplied answers.
Choose B or C. Try the short skill task with usual aids, match the four requirements to what is known and identify one shown skill plus a next step. Keep the model and source card.
Explain why Check is different from not being able to do something. Make the target clearer by naming help, a time and how to check progress. No extra public speech or writing required.

A asked for help when a word was unclear. Which requirement has a clue? A ask for help; B qualification. Key A. Point to the record if unsure and model the match. Keep pictures, plan, words and normal aids; fade answer cues only.

Main: we do not know the qualification. A rule out the route; B ask a trusted adult to help check. Key B. If unclear, contrast missing information with evidence. Parallel: a skill needs practice. A plan a small step with help; B give up the route. Key A. Recheck privately; pass is unobserved.

Cognition and Learning: four short fields, clear model and reduced-choice states. Communication and Interaction: one instruction, pre-taught words, processing time, frames and usual aid. SEMH: calm stages, choice, pass, supported pause/return; no cold calling. Sensory and Physical: large clear text/pictures, pointing instead of moving cards, no colour-only codes. EAL: plan in any language; read and explain requirement words.

Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 provide scaffold/choice; 5 model the first step only, then return task. I Do: locate the clue. We Do: prompt a state choice. You Do: record actual skill evidence and help without completing the checklist for the learner.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write a request or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No personal grades, attendance history, family jobs or finances requested.

Either choice can use Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank fields. Save through the usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show an adult privately. Exact scribe records words/selections, reads back and allows correction. Separate usual access from supplied answers.

Exact source evidence: Requirement-match checklist and one improvement target. Keep selected card, actual ordered response, all four states, one shown requirement and clue, one thing to work on, target/help/time/check, access, prompts, first response, one NS and reply. Judge evidenced strength and next-step identification separately. Usual aids are allowed by the invented skill requirement. Supplied answers do not prove the skill; keep partial evidence and arrange another supported attempt. This is classroom evidence, not proof of real job eligibility.

Unknown does not mean unable. One thing to work on does not close a route. A qualification level on an invented card is not a rule for every job. A completed class task does not prove attendance or a qualification. Shown here records a limited observation; further practice can still be useful.

One NS may add a source clue or make the next step small and checkable. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual banked evidence. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.

All jobs, requirements and the model person are invented. Role types only; no employer, provider, exam board, qualification title or place named. No real entry policy, vacancy or learner record asserted. Do not ask for personal qualifications or attendance. A learner can choose a check as their next step. Staff check actual requirements and available support before real decisions. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures.

H19 requirement matching and target retained. Its RAG checklist uses three labelled states: S Shown here, ? Check, N Next step, with no colour-only meaning or deficit labels. Review is private; K19 websites become prepared cards. Next BUILD Careers Weeks 5–6, one per return; then previously queued LAUNCH Careers Week 1. Further GROW Careers paused. Only Week 4 authored; pause for Downloaded.
Tuesday 26 January 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · BUILD · up to five learners · Spring 1 Week 4 · 25–29 January
Theme: Resilience & Change. Formative. Six weeks; Week 6 assessing.
Students compare their current strengths/qualifications with a realistic course, training or job requirement.
I can identify one requirement I already meet and one thing I may need to work on.

5 arrival/retrieval + 8 I Do + 10 We Do + 12 You Do + 5 review/exit. Model requirement matching with A. Use three labelled states; unknown is not unable. Choose B stockroom or C garden, try the short skill task, make the checklist and set one supported next step.

Same checks for both job cards. One requirement at a time, two states or targets, pictures, words, plan and model. Book, pointing, typing, usual aid or exact scribe. No public questioning or personal records. Trusted adult/help route, pass and supported pause/return.
Requirement-match checklist and one improvement target.
Record one evidenced strength and one next step separately. Keep actual task response, support, target, first response, one NS and reply. Bank in Careers Portfolio; offer to Communication portfolio.
This helps me notice what I can do and ask for help with a next step towards work or training.
BUILD Careers physical row 19 / Spring 1 row 4, E19–N19. Tuesday 26 January 2027 P3. Job cards invented and generic. Next BUILD Careers Week 5 after Downloaded.
Use a made-up job card. Work in your book, point, use your aid, or use Type instead. An adult can read or write your words.
Choose B stockroom or C garden. Try the short task on your card. Use the plan and your usual aid. This is a class task, not a real job check.
List the four needs on the job card. Use S Shown here, ? Check or N Next step. Keep the words with the marks. Do not guess about facts you do not know.
Which need did you show in this task? Keep your work as a clue. “I can ... . My clue is ... .” An adult can help you check it.
Pick one thing to check or practise. “Next lesson, I will ... with ... . I will check ... .” Help and practice can keep a route open.
A asked for help with a word. This shows asking for help. A will try a three-step plan with a word list and a trusted adult next lesson. They will check all three steps.
need · skill · clue · check · help · next step
Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP or ask for a private talk. You may pass or pause. Keep real grades, attendance and private worries out of this work.
Use B or C. Type your own task response and checklist here. Keep personal records and private worries out of this page.
One need I showed here and proof
One thing to check or practise
When and how I will check it
One next step and my reply
States: S Shown here. ? Check. N Next step.
Start: “I can ... . My clue is ... .” “Next lesson, I will ... with ... .”
Save in the usual way with the lesson code and work reference. Show an adult privately. A book, aid or exact scribe is also fine.
Record actual work. No personal records or concerns on this page.
Work reference and selected job card
First response one NS and reply

A pass is unobserved. Do not mark a modelled answer as an independent skill. Keep usual access separate from answer help. E for actual work saved. R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply. Add to Careers Portfolio. Offer to Communication portfolio.
I can identify one requirement I already meet and one thing I may need to work on.

Match a requirement to a relevant clue. A strength and a next step can coexist. The source focus uses gaps; explain it as information to check or a skill to practise, never a deficit label. All job requirements are invented for this task. Do not collect actual attendance or qualification records.

The invented person asked for help with a word: attitude is S Shown here. A has not tried the three-step plan: skill is N Next step. Attendance and qualification are ? Check because no facts are given. The target is practice with a word list and trusted adult next lesson, checking all three cards. No claim about a real person or recruitment rule.

Model check A: asking for help is evidenced. Main hinge B: check an unknown qualification with support. Parallel A: plan a small practice step. Re-model unknown versus evidence if unclear, then recheck privately. Pass is unobserved.

S Shown here needs a relevant clue. ? Check records missing information. N Next step marks an agreed focus for practice or finding out. A Check item can become the selected next-step target without changing the fact that it is unknown. These labels adapt the source RAG structure; no colour-only coding or ranking of learners.

The cards name a generic type or level only. Levels are not qualifications held by the learner. Keep Check unless relevant information is known without collecting personal records; this lesson does not require such evidence. Do not infer attendance from the learner being present today or qualification from completing a task.

Task order: bag, box, tray. An accurate learner-produced order, using the plan and usual aid, can support Shown here for the card’s skill. Record exactly what help was used. Attendance and qualification remain Check. Attitude can be Shown here only if asking for help when unclear was actually observed; otherwise Check. A valid target is practise a new list with an adult and word card next lesson, checking all three labels.

Task order: fill pot, add seed, water. Apply the same evidence rule. This is ordering words, not demonstrating gardening competence. Attendance and qualification remain Check; attitude requires an observation. A valid target is practise a new plan with an adult and word card next lesson, checking all three steps.

A learner may choose to find out what the qualification level means with a trusted adult at the next careers lesson. Keep the answer or unresolved question as the check. Accept a relevant small practice or information target with support. Further practice is valid even after a skill is shown once. Do not invent a weakness just to fill the checklist.
If a skill is not yet shown

Re-read the plan, offer two choices and model the first step only. Record supplied answers. Invite another attempt with usual aids; partial evidence is valid if the learner still cannot show it. An adult-supplied order must not be presented as independent evidence. Use a later supported check rather than forcing a positive judgement.

Record the strength match and next-step identification separately. A shown skill needs an actual clue. The target should relate to the card and say what, help, when and how to check. One NS can add a clue or tighten the target. Retain first response and reply. No inference about real eligibility, worth or future success.

Exact evidence: Requirement-match checklist and one improvement target. Keep actual ordered work, four states, one shown need and clue, one next step, target/help/time/check, access, answer prompts, first response, NS and reply. Partial or unobserved is recorded honestly. No grading of private circumstances.

Evidence Sheet page 2 has blank fields for either job card. Save through usual routine with lesson code and work reference; show privately. Record exact words/selections, read back and permit correction. Book or usual aid is valid. No real application is made.

E means actual evidence banked; R follows Voice, Audience, one NS and the learner’s reply. Add checklist and target to Careers Portfolio; offer to Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping from actual work.

Trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. Pass and supported pause/return remain available. No public questioning or disclosure of real grades, attendance, family work or finances. Listen calmly, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures. Keep concerns outside public evidence.
